rounds.proof_sketch: N=16384 is exactly divisible by TILE_N=64. Grid size is (N+63)/64 = 256 blocks in x-direction. block_col = blockIdx.x * 64 ranges from 0 to 255*64=16320. thread_col = (tid % 16) * 4 ranges from 0 to 60. global_col = block_col + thread_col, max = 16320 + 60 = 16380. col = global_col + j where j ∈ [0,3], so max col = 16380 + 3 = 16383 < 16384 = N. The condition col=N is never reached.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the boundary check from `col < N` to `col <= N` in the write-back loop. However, with the fixed dimensions M=16384, K=16, N=16384, and tile size TILE_N=64, the grid is perfectly sized to cover all N columns. The maximum column index ever computed is 16383 (when blockIdx.x=255, tid%16=15, j=3). Since 16383 < 16384 = N, the original condition `col < N` and the mutated condition `col <= N` both evaluate to true for all reachable col values. The mutation only affects behavior when col equals exactly N, which never occurs under this fixed configuration.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The mutation only changes behavior when col = N = 16384, but the maximum col value ever computed is 16383. Since the shapes are fixed and cannot be changed, there is no value-level input that can trigger the difference between `<` and `<=`.
rounds.recommendations: When writing boundary-condition mutations for GPU kernels, check whether the boundary is actually reachable given the fixed launch configuration. Mutations to conditions involving indices are only killable when the boundary case (here col=N) can actually be reached. This mutant would be killable if N were not perfectly divisible by TILE_N, causing the last tile to potentially access col=N.
